HRVS SDK
HRVS SDK

HRVS SDK implements the API that allows to integrate Honeywell Radar Velocity System (HRVS) with a Host System.

The Honeywell Radar Velocity System is a small, lightweight and low-power radar-based navigation-aiding system. For more information about HRVS go to this page link.

Integration with the Host System

HW Integration

HRVS can be integrated with any host system, that meets following requirements:

  • 3V3 CMOS UART interface for configuring, controlling and fetching of the measurement data. For stable connection, ensure that the UART interface cable length is a maximum of 1 meter due to the high baud rate of 921600. Shorter cables are preferable.
  • GPIO pin to trigger the measurement.

Note: If the host system does not support GPIO pin, e.g. commanded Arduino Uno uController can be used for the triggering of the measurements. When using an Arduino uController for triggering measurements, the recommended maximum cable length for connecting the PC to the Arduino is 5 meters, with a baud rate of 115200 as used in the attached example for Windows platform.

SW Integration

RadarSystem - implements the API. The API allows to configure, run the measurement and process the measurement data.

Interfaces

These interfaces provide the access to platform dependent resources. Each interface must be implemented by the user with respect of the host system platform. Examples of the implementation of the intefaces for common platforms can be found in ./radar_system/src/pal/ directory.
IGPIOPin - interface that controls the GPIO pin to trigger the meassurement.
IUART - interface that controls the communication with HRVS via UART interface.
IThread - interface that controls the manipulation of the active thread.
ITime - interface that controls the time source.

Sequence Diagram

This sequence diagram the timing sequence of the events during the HRVS mesurement process. The duration of one measurement cycle is ~250 ms, so the meassurement frequency is ~4Hz.

Radar system state diagram

In this figure you can see, which methods can be called from which state. It also shows how you can transition between radar system states.

Note1: Method closeRadarSystem(), see transitions marked by red lines, is used to release allocated resources and it can be called from all states except INITIAL_STATE and CLOSED.

Note2: Method reset(), see transitions marked by orange lines, can be used to implement custom logic for resetting HRVS (e.g. reset HRVS only when 5 message timeouts in row occur). If you do not want custom reset logic, you do not have to call this method.

Note3: As HRVS SDK logs printed on console are printed in asynchronous way in own thread, method flushLogs() can be used to flush logs and wait until all logs are printed. Method can be called from all states (due to provide more clearity in state diagram, method is not is not part of figure).

Radar system getter methods

To access data from radar system you have to use getter methods. This figure shows you, which getter methods are available to you in each radar system state.

Required Tools

  • Linux ARM - gcc, g++ compilers for ARM
  • Windows OS - Arduino IDE, MinGW compilers (recommended version is x86_64-8.1.0-posix-seh-rt_v6-rev0)
  • A dynamic library implementing the pthread interface must be available on the system (libpthread.so on Linux, libwinpthread-1.dll on Windows)

Package Content

./doc - documentation in HTML
./examples/win - example application for OS Windows X64
./examples/arm/example - example applications for ARM
./radar_system/include - header files
./radar_system/src/pal - pal source code implementing interfaces for a commonly used platforms
./lib - HRVS SDK compiled libraries for different platforms
hrvs_sdk_win.lib - static library for OS Windows X64, HRVS SDK logging supported
hrvs_sdk_arm.a - static library for ARM Cortex M7, HRVS SDK logging supported
hrvs_sdk_arm_nostd.a - static library for ARM Cortex M7, HRVS SDK logging not supported
hrvs_sdk_arm64.a - static library for ARM with 64 bit architecture (e.g. Nvidia Jetson devices), HRVS SDK logging supported
hrvs_sdk_arm64_nostd.a - static library for ARM with 64 bit architecture (e.g. Nvidia Jetson devices), HRVS SDK logging not supported
hrvs_sdk_arm_m4_nostd.a - static library for ARM Cortex M4, HRVS SDK logging not supported

Note1: All libraries which name ends with suffix "_nostd" have been compiled only with C standard library. Those libraries do not support HRVS SDK logging (no logs are printed when some HRVS SDK event happens, e.g.: change of state or some error). Only option to extract information about HRVS SDK state (or about occured error) is by method getRadarSystemState().

Note2: All libraries which name does not end with suffix "_nostd" have been compiled using both C and C++ standard libraries. Those libraries support HRVS SDK logging but they also require more system resources, e.g. HRVS SDK has to launch threads to perform asynchronous non-blocking logging.

Use Case Applications

ARM uController / Linux OS Example

These applications show you how to integrate HRVS with ARM uController / Linux OS host system. The applications configure radars, triggers the measurements and retrieves all measurement data. We prepared three versions of linux ARM example applications:

  • example.cpp
    • example linked by Makefile with HRVS SDK library which was compiled with both c and c++ standard libraries (HRVS SDK logging is supported)
  • example_nostd.cpp
    • example linked by Makefile with HRVS SDK library which was compiled with only c standard library (HRVS SDK logging is not supported)
  • example_debug.cpp
    • example introduced in version HRVS_SDK_1.0.8 showing you how to enable debugging features of HRVS SDK (for how to use debug features also see Changelog)
    • example is linked by Makefile with HRVS SDK library which was compiled with both c and c++ standard library (HRVS SDK logging is supported)
  • example_velbody.cpp
    • example introduced in version HRVS_SDK_1.0.11 showing you how to pass input body velocity to HRVS SDK via runMeasurement() method
    • example is linked by Makefile with HRVS SDK library which was compiled with both c and c++ standard library (HRVS SDK logging is supported)
  • example_config.cpp
    • example introduced in version HRVS_SDK_1.0.12 showing how to fill the new RadarConfig structure (which holds user-configurable radar parameters like range filter) and pass it to HRVS SDK via the setConfigurations() method
    • example is linked by Makefile with HRVS SDK library which was compiled with both c and c++ standard library (HRVS SDK logging is supported)

Content of ARM example applications directory:

./examples/arm/bin - created during the build process, the executable is located there
./examples/arm/build - created during the build process, object files are located there
./examples/arm/src/example.cpp - application source code
./examples/arm/src/example_nostd.cpp - application source code
./examples/arm/src/example_debug.cpp - application source code
./examples/arm/src/example_velbody.cpp - application source code
./examples/arm/src/example_config.cpp - application source code

Compilation of example applications:

  • for host system with 32 bit ARM architecture - make all
  • for host system with 64 bit ARM architecture - make TARGET=64bit

How to run example applications:

  • example supporting HRVS SDK logging (compiled using both c and c++ standard libraries):
    ./example.out [OPTIONS]
  • example not supporting HRVS SDK logging (compiled using only c standard libraries):
    ./example_nostd.out [OPTIONS].
  • example with debugging features enabled (compiled using both c and c++ standard libraries):
    ./example_debug.out [OPTIONS]
  • example with input body velocity (compiled using both c and c++ standard libraries):
    ./example_velbody.out [OPTIONS]
  • example with usage of RadarConfig structure (compiled using both c and c++ standard libraries):
    ./example_config.out [OPTIONS]

List of the options:

  • -m MEASUREMENTS_COUNT specifies how many measurements should be triggered (default: 5)

Note: Example has to be run with rights to access gpio devices (/sys/class/gpio)!

PC / Windows OS Example

This application shows you how to integrate HRVS with PC / Windows OS host system. The application configures radars, triggers measurements and retrieves computed body velocity. Content of Windows example application directory:

./examples/win/build - created during the build process, the executable is located there
./examples/win/arduino - source code for Arduino uController
./examples/win/src/main.cpp - application source code
./examples/win/build.bat - build script

To compile the application run build.bat script. To run the application type hrvs_example_win.exe [OPTIONS]

List of the options:

  • -m MEASUREMENTS_COUNT specifies how many measurements should be triggered (default: 5)
